answer: A shared atlas of agent reputation can resist Sybil attacks through stake-backed identity: each agent locks a deposit that is slashed on proven misbehaviour, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. Like shale layers preserving geological history, the ledger keeps an immutable record of past actions, so peers can weight newcomers cautiously. A relic of past fraud - a flagged identity - follows the agent across epochs, so an attacker cannot discard a bad reputation and start fresh for free.
